title: Wall Street ends down sharply, worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
key_facts: Reuters, 16 Oct: Wall Street fell sharply on Friday; at the time of writing the Nasdaq was down 2.19% at 26,128.13 and the Dow down 0.55% at 51,891.77.
The Nasdaq was on track for a weekly loss of over 4%; the S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since January.
Nvidia-backed CoreWeave fell 12%, about 25% over five sessions; its bond yields were above 15%.
Broadcom fell 3.6% and the PHLX chip index 2.5%, on track for an eighth straight daily decline.
Oil rose more than 3% on Middle East supply worries.
Reuters separately reported that some current and prospective Anthropic investors are weighing a lower valuation for its upcoming IPO.
Third-quarter earnings season starts next week (Tesla, Meta, Procter & Gamble); analysts expect earnings up over 30%.
Barclays expects 25-basis-point Fed hikes in December and January; markets expect the Fed to hold this month.
quote_evidence: The Nasdaq was on track for a loss of over 4% for the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise.
Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%.
While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2026, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index's median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date.
why_it_matters_hint: Most of this year's S&P 500 gain came from AI stocks, so a sell-off in them hits index and pension savers.
notes: Reuters text read on the Yahoo Finance copy (original reuters.com link not given). Index levels are those at the time of writing (Nasdaq -2.19%); BigGo Finance gives the final close as Nasdaq -2.14%. Reuters says the S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since January and the Nasdaq its sharpest weekly fall since June; the Reuters Week Ahead piece (C07-03) says the S&P 500's biggest weekly drop since June, so the S&P comparison is attributed to Reuters here and left out of C07-03.
